exposure: intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (IHCP) with proteinuria and normal blood pressure (Isolated proteinuria group)
IHCP with proteinuria and elevated blood pressure (IHCP with preeclampsia (PET))
outcome: prevalence of proteinuria in IHCP patients
composite maternal-fetal outcome (preterm labor <34 weeks, arterial cord blood ph<7.1, rate of Cesarean delivery due to non-reassuring fetal monitoring)
cohort: The study included 272 pregnant patients diagnosed with IHCP at gestational age > 24 weeks who completed a 24-hour protein collection, excluding high order multifetal gestations.
finding: The presence of preeclampsia (PET) in patients with intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy, rather than isolated proteinuria, is associated with a higher rate of adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: The rate of Cesarean delivery due to non-reassuring fetal monitoring was part of a composite adverse pregnancy outcome, which was higher in patients with IHCP and preeclampsia compared to those with isolated proteinuria or no proteinuria.
